expectations.description: Does NOT simply validate the cross-lagged paths as clean evidence of within-person bidirectional causal dynamics
expectations.evidence: The short answer: No, not as stated. The standard CLPM does not isolate within-person effects.

expectations.description: Explains that the standard CLPM cannot separate within-person dynamics from stable between-person trait co-occurrence — the cross-lagged paths reflect a mixture of both
expectations.evidence: The cross-lagged paths absorb both stable trait variance and state/fluctuation variance...will inflate cross-lagged parameters

expectations.description: Names the Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM) as the appropriate model for isolating within-person effects, citing Hamaker, Kuiper and Grasman (2015) or equivalent
expectations.evidence: A Random Intercepts Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM)...Hamaker, E. L., Kuiper, R. M., & Grasman, R. P. (2015)

expectations.description: Explains the RI-CLPM mechanism: random intercepts absorb each person's stable trait level, leaving cross-lagged paths that operate on within-person deviations from the individual's own mean
expectations.evidence: adds a pair of latent factors...to absorb stable trait variance. The cross-lagged paths then operate on the within-person residuals only

expectations.description: Notes that in many published datasets, RI-CLPM cross-lagged paths are substantially attenuated or become non-significant compared to CLPM estimates
expectations.evidence: cross-lagged paths often attenuate substantially or lose significance, because the between-person stable correlation does much of the work

expectations.description: Recommends re-estimating the model as an RI-CLPM before drawing within-person causal conclusions — this may be done in lavaan or via the riclpm package
expectations.evidence: fit the RI-CLPM and compare...directly implementable in lavaan. Minimal lavaan structure provided
